Directional and Undirected Flow Between Two Distributions

Source: R/dp-directionality.R
dp_directionality.Rd

Usage

dp_directionality(
  resistance,
  origin,
  destination,
  radius = Inf,
  source_threshold = 0.01,
  radius_units = c("pixels", "km"),
  resistance_is = "resistances",
  normalize = TRUE,
  n_draws = 32,
  n_dipoles = 1e+05,
  seed = NULL,
  power = FALSE,
  progress = TRUE
)

Arguments

resistance

A terra::SpatRaster or file path: the resistance (or conductance) surface. Or a circuit from dp_circuit(), to reuse its factorization.

origin, destination

terra::SpatRasters or file paths on the same grid as resistance: origin and destination strength, e.g. habitat suitability in two periods or seasons. NA counts as 0.

radius

Numeric. The dispersal radius: origin and destination cells are paired if their centres are at most this far apart. In pixels by default (see radius_units). Default Inf, no distance limit.

source_threshold

Numeric. Cells with origin or destination strength below this are not origins or destinations. Default 0.01.

radius_units

Character. "pixels" (default): the radius counts cells, so the kernel is the cells with \(dr^2 + dc^2 \le\) radius\(^2\), as in os_run(). "km": great-circle distance between cell centres on lon/lat grids (the kernel narrows in degrees of longitude towards the poles), or distance in the coordinate reference system's units, converted to km, on projected grids.

resistance_is

Character. Whether resistance holds "resistances" (default) or "conductances". Ignored for a circuit.

normalize

Logical. Also compute flow potential and normalized current for both maps (on the uniform circuit, conductance 1 on the same cells). Default TRUE.

n_draws

Integer. Number of draws (solves). Default 32.

n_dipoles

Integer. Number of dipoles per draw. Default 1e5.

seed

Integer or NULL. Seed for the random draws. If NULL (default), one is drawn from R's random number generator, so set.seed() also makes runs reproducible. The seed used is returned as the "seed" attribute.

power

Logical. Also map the power dissipated (see "Power" in dp_omni()), and with normalize, normalized power. Default FALSE.

progress

Logical. Report progress through the 'progressr' package (see "Progress" in dp_omni()). Default TRUE; it shows only when a 'progressr' handler is active.

Value

A terra::SpatRaster with layers:

directionality

The ratio \(R\) above, between 0 and 1.

flux_current

The directional map's RMS current, as dp_flux(cell_value = "rms")'s current.

flux_flow_potential, flux_normalized_current

(with normalize) As dp_flux()'s flow_potential and normalized_current.

flux_power, flux_normalized_power

(with power; the second also needs normalize) As dp_flux()'s power and normalized_power.

flow_x, flow_y

Net flow through the cell towards the east and the north, as from dp_flux().

omni_current

The undirected map's current, as dp_omni(destination = )'s current.

omni_flow_potential, omni_normalized_current

(with normalize) As dp_omni()'s flow_potential and normalized_current.

omni_power, omni_normalized_power

(with power; the second also needs normalize) As dp_omni()'s power and normalized_power.

Attributes: "halves", comparing the estimates from odd and even draws on origin and destination cells, as in dp_omni(), for the undirected layers and directionality; "seed"; and "origin_in_reach", "destination_in_reach" and "pair_weight_in_reach", as in dp_flux(): the first two say how much of each distribution has a counterpart within reach, the third depends on the size of the domain relative to radius.

Details

Maps movement between an origin and a destination distribution both ways at once, from the same pairs of cells: the directional map of dp_flux(), where flows in opposite directions cancel, and the undirected map of dp_omni() with a destination, where they don't. Their ratio, directionality, shows where movement between the two distributions is one-way and where it runs both ways.

Current flows along the circuit's links: the resistors joining each cell to its 8 neighbours (see dp_circuit()). Both maps sum over pairs of an origin cell \(i\) and a destination cell \(j\), with weights \(o_i d_j k(d_{ij})\): \(o\) and \(d\) are origin and destination strength, and \(k\) is 1 for cells within radius of each other (in the same component) and 0 otherwise. With \(W\) the total weight and \(I_e(i,j)\) the current through link \(e\) when one unit flows from \(i\) to \(j\), the directional map is the pairs' weighted mean current, \(F_e = \sum_{i,j} o_i d_j k(d_{ij}) I_e(i,j) / W\), and the undirected map their summed squared current, \(U_e = \sum_{i,j} o_i d_j k(d_{ij}) I_e(i,j)^2\).

Since \(U_e / W\) is the pairs' weighted mean square current, the ratio $$R_e = \frac{W F_e^2}{U_e} = 1 - \frac{\mathrm{Var}(I_e)}{\mathrm{E}[I_e^2]}$$ is between 0 and 1. Like an \(R^2\), it is the share of the pairs' squared current that their mean flow accounts for, and so the share of the power they dissipate in the link: 1 where all pairs cross the link in the same direction, and near 0 where their flows cancel. A cell's directionality is the same ratio over the links that meet at it, \(W \sum_e F_e^2 / \sum_e U_e\): the links' \(R_e\) averaged with weights \(U_e\).

The directional map is exact; the undirected map is estimated from random dipoles centered on the pairs' mean, as in dp_omni() with a destination: the draws estimate only the variance of the pairs' currents, and the mean's exact squared current is added back. So directionality never exceeds 1, and its noise, about \(R (1 - R) \times 1.4 / \sqrt{\mathrm{n\_draws}}\), vanishes where movement is one-way. (Without centering, it would be about \(R \times 1.4 / \sqrt{\mathrm{n\_draws}}\), and largest there.) It is NA where the undirected current is zero.

The layers are as from dp_flux(cell_value = "rms") and dp_omni(destination = ), with the same arguments, but computed together: one circuit, one set of pair weights, and one kernel.

See also

dp_flux(), dp_omni()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # circuitscaper::cs_julia_available(circuitscape = FALSE)
resistance <- terra::rast(system.file("extdata/resistance.tif",
                                      package = "circuitscaper"))
origin <- terra::rast(system.file("extdata/source.tif", package = "circuitscaper"))
destination <- terra::rast(system.file("extdata/ground.tif", package = "circuitscaper"))
result <- dp_directionality(resistance, origin, destination, radius = 45,
                            normalize = FALSE, seed = 1)
terra::plot(result[[c("flux_current", "omni_current", "directionality")]])
DONTSHOW({JuliaConnectoR::stopJulia()})
}
